### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **6** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/driver-turso`, `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **107** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/index.ts`, `packages/mcp/src/index.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**52** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ba6556c617bc201f1d4b635c609b28b589583c36`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/index.ts`, `packages/mcp/src/index.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `findData (4 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `owner_id (literal, 43 pages)`
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **59** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ba6556c617bc201f1d4b635c609b28b589583c36` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `aef3a0d6acac5ac50c523b0307a8fe9181c1dcbb` — the merge of head `303482dda2b7d2aebe857f06b5ef9b4b709daad4` into base `ba6556c617bc201f1d4b635c609b28b589583c36`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin aef3a0d6acac5ac50c523b0307a8fe9181c1dcbb && git checkout aef3a0d6acac5ac50c523b0307a8fe9181c1dcbb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ba6556c617bc201f1d4b635c609b28b589583c36 303482dda2b7d2aebe857f06b5ef9b4b709daad4 && git checkout -B drift-repro ba6556c617bc201f1d4b635c609b28b589583c36 && git merge --no-ff 303482dda2b7d2aebe857f06b5ef9b4b709daad4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ba6556c617bc201f1d4b635c609b28b589583c36
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ba6556c617bc201f1d4b635c609b28b589583c36` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `303482dda2b7d2aebe857f06b5ef9b4b709daad4`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #35145 (body, triage 6972038283, claim 6973844822, amendment 6974061928, the two regrades, os-dev-report 6979530359), PR #35199 (body, 27-file list, net diff against `main` at this head), and the 52 check-runs on this head. At review time 17 had concluded success, 15 were skipped and 20 were still in progress: Test Core 1-10, Build Core, Build Docs, Live E2E UI, the five Lint families, the two scoped lints, and Type Check workspace, consumer and debt. None had failed. Those conclusions are the gate verdicts. This record does not stand in for them, and the seat's ACCEPT waits on them.

### ① Derived judgments

Public surface, each change judged:

- **`query_records` input gains `latestPer`** (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`). It is a strict object with `by` (1 to 3 non-empty strings) and `orderBy` (1 to 3 strict `{ field, order: asc|desc }`). This is an additive accept-set: every call that was valid before is still valid and answered the same way, because the `latestPer === undefined` arm is the old code unchanged. **Right.** The bounds match the engine's `LATEST_PER_MAX_KEYS`, and the engine checks the shape again (`assertLatestPerShape`).
- **`query_records` answer under `latestPer`** is `{ object, records, hasMore }`, never a `total`, plus `truncated: true` set by the shared `servedQueryPage` from the door's `hasMore`. The row cap is the tool's own: `page = min(limit ?? maxLimit, maxLimit)`. The door reads `limit + 1` groups and does not serve the extra one. This is the card's "same row cap and `truncated` contract". **Right.** `latestPerAnswer` turns a bridge answer that is not a group page (one that carries `total`, or lacks a boolean `hasMore`) into a coded 500, so it is never passed on as a list. Fail-closed. **Right.**
- **`McpDataBridge.query` opts gains optional `latestPer`**, and a new exported type `McpLatestPer` is added. An optional input member breaks no implementer. A host bridge that ignores the member and answers a plain list with `total` is refused by `latestPerAnswer`. **Right** (see the nit in ③).
- **New exports.** `@objectstack/objectql` exports `LATEST_PER`, `LATEST_PER_MAX_KEYS` and the types `LatestPerRequest`, `LatestPerOrder` and `LatestPerOutcome`. `@objectstack/driver-sql` exports `LATEST_PER_DIRECTIVE`, `latestPerDirectiveOf` and the types `LatestPerDirective` and `LatestPerDirectiveOrder`. All are additive. **Right.** Both keys are `Symbol.for` symbols and are never wire or `QueryAST` keys. `@objectstack/spec` is unchanged, and the claim amendment's "no spec member" line holds.
- **`findData` (metadata-protocol)** gains an in-process symbol member on its request. There is no wire change, because a JSON body cannot carry a symbol. **Right.**

Read-path bound: is every row the new shape returns held to the same walls a plain `query_records` read applies? Judged against the code at this head:

- **Tenant wall.** The driver's outer `find` statement is unchanged: `applyTenantScope` + `applyFilters(where)`. It gains one predicate, `id IN (SELECT id FROM (SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (...) FROM t WHERE ...) w WHERE rn = 1)`. The inner select runs `applyTenantScope` with the read's own `options` and `applyFilters` with the same final `where` (`sql-driver-latest-per.ts`). Every returned row still passes the outer wall. The window also chooses only among in-tenant rows, so another organization's newer row cannot win a group and blank it. **Holds.** The driver test and the dogfood two-org wall pin it, with armed controls.
- **RLS, sharing and composed scopes.** The directive is attached in `engine-find.ts` after `composeReadableIdsAtBoundary`, on the AST that has already passed the doors, the middleware chain and `beforeFind`. Its `where` therefore carries every composed scope. The inner predicate set equals the outer one (tenant + final `where`), so the winner of a group is always a row the outer statement admits. There is no "group vanishes because a hidden row won" inference channel. **Holds.** The dogfood "hidden newest answers newest visible" test and its armed RLS control pin it.
- **Field-level read judgement, partition and order keys included.** In `engine.find`, every partition and order field the caller's own `orderBy` does not already name is appended to `ast.orderBy` before the doors run: `rejectInternalFieldEvaluation`, `rejectCredentialEvaluation`, `assertOrderByIsMaterializable` and the middleware chain. They are taken back off only in `withLatestPerDirective` at the executor boundary. plugin-security's predicate guard (`collectQueryFields`, `orderBy[].field`) rejects with 403 on a non-readable field and never strips one. A field the caller may not read is therefore refused, not silently dropped while the directive still windows on it. **Holds.** The dogfood `PERMISSION_DENIED` case pins it. The ingress doors judge the same keys:
  - `findData` uses `assertSortFieldsExist(..., 'latestPer')`, which covers unknown, dotted, unmaterialisable and `sortable: false` fields, plus the stored-metadata body/hash sort refusal and `assertNoInternalFieldEvaluated`.
  - The stdio bridge applies the body, hash and `unofferedSortRefusal` checks over `judgedOrderBy`.
  - The engine itself refuses formula, structured-JSON, multi-value and dotted fields as `INVALID_FIELD`.
  
  Returned rows go through the unchanged masking path. The withheld-field case in the dogfood test pins it.
- **Every refusal fires before any read.** At the top of `engine.find`, before `resolveWhereTokens` and the chain, the engine refuses: the shape, a driver outside the named allowlist, a federated object, an `afterFind` hook (`hasHooksFor`, wildcard-matching), object-keyed middleware, and the field kinds above. `findData` refuses unknown or unsortable keys and `latestPer` combined with `groupBy`/aggregations before the engine. The MCP `readGuard` runs first. The Turso remote face refuses the directive in the driver too, before any statement. **Holds.** Two exits come after a read, and both are faults, not request refusals:
  - The `outcome !== 'served'` 500, fired by the protocol, runtime and stdio layers.
  - The "planned read cannot carry a latest-per request" invariant, which fires after `composeReadableIdsAtBoundary`.
  
  Neither serves rows. **Right.**
- **Dialects.** The allowlist admits the driver-sql name for every dialect it speaks. MSSQL and Oracle are federation-only families in driver-sql, and federated objects are refused, so only SQLite, Postgres and MySQL 8 managed tables reach the window. The `CASE WHEN ... IS NULL` key, the derived-table alias and the quoted `??` identifiers are valid on all three. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

The changeset `.changeset/35145-mcp-latest-per.md` lists `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/driver-turso`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/runtime`, all at `patch`. That set is exactly the released packages whose `src` this diff changes outside tests. `driver-sqlite-wasm` gets only a test, `packages/qa/dogfood` is a test, `scripts/` and `content/docs` do not publish, and `skip-changeset` is correctly absent.

Both declaration lines appear, line-initial, in the PR body and the changeset body:
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)`
- `Metadata-protocol: none`

These are right. The change adds a read form on the published MCP tool surface and new exports, and it adds no spec key, no accepted metadata value and no metadata type. The AGENTS.md changeset rule then ships a non-protocol widening as `patch`. **`patch` matches what the diff publishes.** There is no breaking arm, so no migration text or ADR-0087 marker is owed. `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head.

Clause-②: yes (widening): matches the diff. A published MCP tool input is widened, and every pre-existing call is unchanged.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: `[]` in os-dev-report 6979530359. Nothing is owed.
- `security_findings`: none declared. None found in this review.
- Dev deviation (1): a one-line `DECLARED_WATCH_HINTS` entry in `scripts/check-tenant-chokepoint.mjs` for the new `sql-driver-latest-per.ts`. This is outside the amended file surface. **Answered, accepted.** It widens what the tenant-chokepoint gate watches to cover a new module that calls `applyTenantScope`, and the gate's self-test demands it. Nothing is loosened.
- Dev deviation (2): the `driver-sqlite-wasm` test file. **Answered, accepted.** The amendment admits that package for its allowlist entry, and the test pins exactly that.
- Dev deviation (3): `Part of #35145` in place of `Refs #35145`. **Answered, accepted.** Both are non-closing, and the card stays open for PR 2. `PR-body guards` concluded success.
- MySQL not measured locally. CI's live-dialect job runs on push and schedule, not on this PR, and `Temporal Conformance` is skipped here. **Answered, not blocking.** The statement uses MySQL 8 features the repo already targets, and the cell runs on the first push to `main`. The seat should read that run after landing.
- Overlap with open PRs #35179 and #35193 in `mcp-http-tools.ts`. **Answered.** Whichever lands second merges `main`, per the claim.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): **no finding.** One row per group is computed in one SQL statement as a `ROW_NUMBER()` window inside an `id IN` subquery. No id list is materialised in the app, no in-app join or dedupe runs, the group probe is `limit + 1` in SQL, and no COUNT is run. Drivers that cannot push it down are refused, not approximated.
- Nit, no effect on the contract: `outcome = 'served'` is stamped when `driver.find` returns on an allowlisted driver. It attests the engine path, not that the driver compiled the directive. The driver ablation pins the compile, and a symbol-stripping wrapper between engine and driver would degrade the answer, not the walls.
- Nit: `findLatestPer` takes a server probe limit (`listPlan.probe`, a row budget with no page size) as the group page and skips `assertQueryReadRows`. This is unreachable from the MCP door, which always sends `limit`.
- Nit: `latestPerAnswer` recognises a non-group answer by shape (`total` present or `hasMore` not boolean). A third-party bridge that ignores `latestPer` and answers `{ records, hasMore }` without `total` would pass. Both in-repo bridges serve it.
- Pre-existing, outside diff: none named.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-35145-mcp-latest-per-and-related-read`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JQwxbaX2qDxUq9sF93EqqL`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对

**L1 full · ACCEPT** · Head-sha: `303482dda2b7d2aebe857f06b5ef9b4b709daad4` · card #35145 (`Part of #35145`, PR 1 of 2) · read 2026-11-18T13:44Z

Net diff against merge base `c787255a49`: 27 files, +1971 / -30. Not governed. It reads under row and field security.

### Against the card

- **`Part of` is right.** This PR carries the card's "latest per group" half: one bounded read on `query_records`, under the caller's row and field security, with the list cap and the `truncated` contract, and a stable refusal where a driver cannot compile it. The related-objects read and the ask-card kinds (#35113) stay for PR 2, so the merge must not close the card.
- **The card's "reading first" item is answered in the body.** The engine had no one-statement form, so the SQL drivers compile a `ROW_NUMBER()` window, and every other driver refuses with no slower in-memory path, as the card asks.
- **File surface.** The source is in the claimed packages. Three items are declared deviations: the one `DECLARED_WATCH_HINTS` row in `scripts/check-tenant-chokepoint.mjs` (the new driver file reads the tenant scope, so the gate's own self-test asks for it), the sqlite-wasm test, and the `Part of` spelling. I accept all three.

### Rules checked at the head

- **The choice runs over the caller's own rows.**
  - The engine attaches the window directive only at the executor boundary, on the AST that `composeReadableIdsAtBoundary` returns, after the doors, the middleware chain and `beforeFind`.
  - In the driver, the window subquery applies the same `applyTenantScope` and the same `applyFilters(query.where)` as the outer statement, so the row that wins a group is chosen only from rows the composed read admits.
  - The outer statement keeps its own tenant scope, `where`, ORDER BY, projection, limit and offset.
  - The dogfood case pins the property end to end: a row policy hides a group's newest row, and the answer is that group's newest readable row, never the hidden one and never an empty group.
- **The partition and order fields pass every sort gate.**
  - On the HTTP door, `findData` runs them through `assertSortFieldsExist`. That covers unknown, dotted and unmaterializable fields, and fields declared `sortable: false`. They also go through the stored-body and stored-hash predicate refusals and the internal-field gate.
  - In the engine they are appended to the AST's `orderBy` before the secret-field gate and the middleware chain run, so the field-security predicate guard refuses a hidden field exactly as it refuses one in `orderBy`. They are taken back off only at the boundary.
  - On stdio they join the stored-body, stored-hash and `sortable` verdicts.
  - The engine also refuses formula, JSON, multi-value and dotted fields as partition or order keys.
- **Refusal before any read.** The engine refuses with `INVALID_QUERY` / 400 before anything is read in each of these cases:
  - a driver outside the allowlist (the SQL driver, sqlite-wasm, and Turso only on its local or replica face),
  - a federated object (so the federation-only SQL dialects never reach the window),
  - an object with an `afterFind` hook or object-keyed read middleware, where a group could lose its answer after the driver chose it.

  Turso's remote face also refuses the directive itself. A planned (semi-join) read cannot carry it.
- **The request is in-process only.** It rides `Symbol.for('objectstack.objectql.latestPer')` from the MCP bridges through `callData` and `findData` to `find`. It is never a wire or query key, so no REST caller can reach it.
- **An unserved read is never passed off as an answer.** The engine marks `outcome: served` only after the driver answered the window. `findData`, `callData` and the stdio bridge each refuse a read without that mark. The tool layer refuses a bridge answer that is not one page of groups, or that carries a `total`.
- **Paging.** `limit` counts groups, and the tool caps it at `maxLimit`. The doors read `limit + 1` and answer `hasMore`, with no `total` and no COUNT. `truncated: true` comes from the shared `servedQueryPage`, and a plain `query_records` call keeps its own probe unchanged.
- **The MCP read guard** still judges `objectName` first. `latestPer` reaches no object other than the one named.
- **Tests.** The live dialect matrix covers SQLite, Postgres and MySQL (MySQL in CI's live-dialect job). There are also the engine refusal table, the `findData` door, the tool bounds, the sqlite-wasm and Turso-remote suites, and the CRM dogfood over `/mcp` with a real two-organization wall and armed controls. The driver ablation turns five pins red and keeps the three that do not depend on the predicate green.

### Declarations, docs, merge

- **Changeset, read sentence by sentence.** Six packages, all `patch`. `Clause-②: yes (widening)`: a new optional tool argument and new exports, and every read without `latestPer` is unchanged. `Metadata-protocol: none`, and `@objectstack/spec` is untouched. Each bullet matches the code (bounds, tie and null order, the choice over readable rows, the refusals, the paging contract, the exports).
- **`connect-mcp.mdx`.** The new section says what the code does. Its driver list names the dialects the driver serves to managed objects (Oracle and SQL Server are federation-only per `drivers.mdx`, and federated objects are refused). No existing sentence becomes false.
- **Merges** cleanly onto origin/main `ba6556c617`.
- **Check-runs at this head:** 55 in total, all completed, none failed (40 `success`, 15 `skipped`).

### Nits (none blocks)

- `findLatestPer` reads `findQuery.limit` as the group page. It ignores whether the list plan set that limit as a server probe (a row budget with no page size). The MCP tools always pass a limit, so no caller reaches that case today. A later in-process caller would.
- The window's `ORDER BY` puts empty values last with a `CASE` per key, which a plain index on the order column does not cover. That is fine at `limit + 1` groups, but worth knowing for large partitions.

### Not mine, still owed before landing

- **L2 at `TIER_DEFAULT`** (running).
- **Sequencing.** #35179 and #35193 conflict with this PR in `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`. Whichever lands second merges main.
